name: Victorian sanitary ware
summary: The first ceramic bathroom of the home. Basins, pans and cisterns of earthenware and early vitreous china carry blue, brown or polychrome transfer prints, moulded flowers and gilt lines.

philosophy.core_thesis: A new sanitary fitting must look like fine china, so that a family sees a clean, rich object in a room that was once hidden.
design_principles: Cover each visible face with a transfer print in one to three colours, such as blue, brown or green.
Mould a raised flower, a shell or a dolphin into the rim, the handle and the pedestal.
Glaze the bowl white and thick, 0.5 to 1 mm, so that it is easy to clean.
Fit the wash-down pan with a plain curved trap, so that 9 litres of water clear the bowl.
Shape the basin with a wide rim, 3 tap holes and a small overflow slot at the back.
Mount the cistern high on the wall with a pull chain of brass and a porcelain handle.
Add gilt lines on the rim of a fine basin only, as the last firing.
anti_patterns: A plain white bowl with no print and no moulded detail
A bright coloured glaze all over the body
A thin sheet that cracks at the rim
A wall-hung pan with a hidden cistern
A matte surface that holds dirt

form.shape: Pedestal and bracket washbasins, wash-down pans with a high flared rim, high-level cisterns, and cased baths.
form.profile: A bowl with a deep curve and a rolled rim, resting on a fluted pedestal or a cast iron frame with a scroll.
form.foot_and_rim: A wide, flat rim with a moulded edge, a lipped front on the pan, and a flat base that stands on the floor.
form.proportion: Basin 550 to 650 mm wide and 12 mm thick at the wall; pan seat height 380 to 420 mm.
rules: Print the pattern in a band that follows the rim and the bowl.
Mould the relief in the same casting, not applied later.
Keep the trap and the pan in one piece, so that there is no joint in the bowl.
Choose the pattern of the basin and the pan from the same set.

bodies.rule: Use a thick, cream or white body that takes a printed pattern, and after 1880 a dense vitreous body that does not hold water.

forming.joins: The pedestal and the basin join in a plaster mould before the firing; brass taps and chains are fitted after the last firing.
forming.details: A maker's name moulded under the rim, a registration lozenge in raised letters, and a small spur mark on the base.

glaze.pattern: Stylised flowers, ferns, birds and Japanese-style fans in a band under the rim, and a large flower or a scene in the bowl of a pan.
glaze.gloss: High gloss, about 80 to 95 GU, with a smooth, even clear glaze over the print.
glaze.wear: Fine crazing lines appear in the glaze, and the gilt wears at the rim; the print under the glaze stays sharp.

palette.strategy: A white ground with one printed colour in blue, brown or green, and a few polychrome pieces with gilt.

firing.kiln: A coal-fired bottle oven with saggars, one firing for the biscuit and one for the glost.
processes: gilt and a third firing at 750 °C
firing.scale: Staffordshire and London potteries with hundreds of workers; one works makes many hundreds of pans in a week.
firing.signs: A stilt mark inside the foot, a print seam where the paper overlaps, and a registration mark on the underside.

pieces.form: Pedestal basin with a blue print of ferns and a moulded rim
Wash-down pan with a flared rim and a printed flower in the bowl
High-level cistern with a moulded shell and a brass pull chain
Cased fireclay bath with a roll rim and a white glaze
Basin with a gilt rim line and polychrome flowers

positive: high-level cistern with a brass pull chain

canonical_works.work: Public retiring rooms at the Great Exhibition

emotion.target_response: A proud, clean domestic order: the viewer sees a room that shows its water supply as an object of pride.

use_cases: a period bathroom set for a film or a game
an interior brief for a Victorian house
a museum label on an early flush toilet
avoid_when: the brief wants a plain white modern bathroom
the brief wants a coloured 1950s suite

modifiers.how: Remove the print and the relief, shape the bowl as a tight rectangle, and hang it on the wall.
Replace the printed pattern by one even coloured gloss and keep the moulded shape.

wall_thickness.note: Early earthenware basins are thicker than later vitreous pieces.
